Glaze Search · which model for which input

Version 2026-11-06 (v1)colour match 70cd01c0c673smart search 78afd7dfbe2c 395 held-out recipes · 6,625 searchedapp: Auto engine, configs/glaze_decision.json

A decision record: what the updated test_similarity (3).zip contains, whether anything in it should be trained again or added to the app, how its model compares with smart search and with two hybrids on recipes that no model trained on, and which engine the app should use for each kind of input. Every number below comes from python scripts/eval_glaze_engines.py (133 s on the CPU).

The decision in short
  • No new model in test_similarity (3). Its 3 model files are byte-identical to (2) and to the installed model (fingerprint 70cd01c0c673); latent_space.py is a report on that same model. Nothing needs training again.
  • Photo, words or formula given → Smart search, by a wide margin on every measure that finds the recipe (e.g. typed sentence R@10 0.79 vs colour match 0.43).
  • Hybrid (smart + the colour-match learned match): not adopted. Its best weight was 0 and 0.05 on the two halves: adding the colour-match match does not help smart search.
  • Colour match + a new image head: the colour-match space can take a cut-out photo (photo R@10 0.19 → 0.27), but it stays below smart search (0.45). Experiment only.
  • Only a colour → colour ranking without a learned model (CIEDE2000 + cone + surface). There both learned models lose: MRR 0.136 vs smart 0.113 and colour match 0.079; same colour in the top 10 0.88 vs 0.59.
  • Colour + menus only → Colour match: With only the colour, cone and surface menus, colour match gives the most results with both the same colour and the same surface (63 % vs 54 % smart search); it finds the exact recipe a little less often (MRR 0.31 vs 0.34).
  • The app now has an Auto engine (default on card G) that applies this tree; Smart search and Colour match stay as buttons.

3 · Evaluation: every engine on recipes no model trained on

Set-up. Test recipes: in the colour-match test split and in the joint model's validation or test split, with a measured colour: 395 recipes. Every recipe of both catalogs can be found (6,625). Each test recipe is asked six ways (below). Its colour is moved by a random CIELAB offset (sd 3 per channel, median ΔE00 3.7), as a new photo of the same glaze would be. In the photo queries the query object is removed from the recipe's own gallery embedding (leave-one-object-out; rebuilt embeddings match the installed ones, cosine 1.000000). The two hybrid weights are cross-fitted: chosen on one half of the test recipes (split by composition group), scored on the other half.
Measures. R@1 / R@10: the true recipe at #1 / in the top 10 (random R@10 = 0.0015). MRR: mean of 1 / rank. Same chemistry: a recipe in the top 10 whose square-root oxide fractions have cosine ≥ 0.99 with the true one. Same colour: ΔE00 ≤ 10 to the true colour. Colour AND surface: both at once. Differences with a paired bootstrap (2,000 resamples), 95 % interval.

the engine Auto uses for this inputother engines · each panel shows the measure that decides that input: what the input asks for (only a colour → the same colour; colour + menus → the same colour and surface; a photo, words or formula → the right recipe)

Hybrid: adding the colour-match learned match to smart search

Every line falls as the colour-match part gets more weight: the learned match adds no information that smart search does not already have. Chosen weight on each half: 0 and 0.05 (best on all test recipes: 0).

The colour-match space with a cut-out photo (new image head)

One linear layer (DINOv2 1,024 → 256, like the colour-match heads) trained on the colour-match train recipes only (4,145 objects) against the frozen colour-match chemistry vectors, masked InfoNCE (temperature 0.07), early stop on 281 held-out recipes: photo → own chemistry R@10 0.379 (random 0.036) after 31 epochs (1.6 s). The team's model is not changed. Added to colour match with weight 0.4 (cross-fitted): photo R@10 0.19 → 0.27, photo + words 0.43 → 0.48. Smart search: 0.45 and 0.84. So the answer to "can the text–chemistry space take cropped images?" is yes, and a photo even aligns with chemistry better than the template text does, but the combined engine is still well below smart search. The head is kept with the evaluation (work/eval/glaze_engines_2026-11-06.image_head.pt), not installed.

Robustness: does the decision hold?

For each way of asking: the engine Auto uses vs the best other engine, under no colour noise, the main noise, double noise, and on the recipes whose colour is the same in both catalogs (the query colour comes from the joint model's palette, so there no engine has a home advantage). The first row of each input is the measure that decides it. Green = the chosen engine is best or within 0.005 (tie); orange = another engine is better on that measure. The hybrid is left out here: with its cross-fitted weight (0–0.05) it is smart search itself. Two kinds of orange are expected: the menus MRR (the trade-off stated in the decision) and the no colour noise column, where the query colour is exactly the colour stored for the recipe, so an engine that leans on colour finds the recipe from its colour alone. No new photo gives the exact stored colour: that column is a stress test, not the main result.

4 · The latent-space report (latent_space.py), in context

Numberlatent_space.py (folder of (3))Evaluation PDF (D4)Meaning
text → own chemistry R@10, test7.0 % (1,309; same-group recipes not masked)8.2 % (same-group excluded)same model, slightly stricter count; random 0.8 %
cosine, right pair vs random pair0.238 vs 0.079 (test)0.238 vs 0.076about 3× apart: learned, but weak
effective dimensionstext 20.1 · chemistry 12.5 of 256–the chemistry side passes PCA-16, so it can use at most 16 directions
modality gapcentres cosine 0.515–text and chemistry vectors sit in two separate clouds (figure below, left)

The template text is short and repeats: 3,878 different sentences for 6,718 recipes; 3,662 recipes share their exact sentence with another recipe. No model can tell those recipes apart from the text, which caps the learned match. In section 3 this shows: at finding the right recipe, colour match ranks below the same ranking with its learned part switched off (colour ranking minus colour match, MRR: colour only +0.058, menus +0.034, words +0.034, typed +0.035). What the learned part does add: results a little closer in chemistry (colour only: 0.898 vs 0.890) and, because the template text names the surface, many more results with the asked surface. That is why it gives the best colour-and-surface list when only the menus are used (0.63 vs 0.55).
